questions: What is the exact definition of coprime positive integers P and Q when expressing a rational number x as P/Q?
How should the function f(x) handle cases where x is already an integer (i.e., when Q=1)?
Are there any additional constraints on the sequence S elements beyond being positive integers?
What is the precise mathematical proof that guarantees there are finitely many good sequences?
How should ties or equivalent sequences be handled when calculating the final sum of scores?
Is the gcd condition applied to the entire sequence S after determining all elements, or incrementally during construction?
What is the expected behavior when A_i = 1 for some indices, making P×Q = 1?
Should the empty product (when N=1) be considered as contributing 1 to the sum, or is N≥2 guaranteed by the constraints?
answers: P and Q are coprime means gcd(P,Q)=1, the standard definition.
If x is an integer, Q=1 and P=x, so f(x)=x.
Not specified beyond being positive integers satisfying the given divisibility and gcd conditions.
Not detailed beyond what's given; the finiteness follows from the given conditions but isn't elaborated further.
Not applicable; there's no notion of ties, just a sum over all valid sequences.
The gcd condition applies to the sequence S as a whole, evaluated once all elements are determined.
When A_i=1, f(S_i/S_{i+1})=1 forces P=Q=1 in lowest terms, i.e. S_i=S_{i+1}.
Not applicable; N is guaranteed to be at least 2 per the constraints.

For a positive rational number x, define f(x) as follows:
Express x as $\dfrac{P}{Q}$ using coprime positive integers P and Q. f(x) is defined as the value P\times Q. P and Q are coprime means gcd(P,Q)=1, the standard definition.
You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_{N-1}) of positive integers of length N-1.
We call a sequence S=(S_1,S_2,\dots,S_N) of positive integers of length N a good sequence if it satisfies all of the following conditions:
- For every integer i with 1\leq i\leq N-1, it holds that f$\left(\dfrac{S_i}{S_{i+1}}\right)$=A_i.
- $\gcd(S_1,S_2,\dots,S_N)$=1.
